findings.statement: Official API scan with the keywords x-ray animal, inside insect, how it works 3d, microscopic world, animal anatomy returned 44 qualified outliers from 50 candidates with 0 errors.

Monarch Cam currently has 3.82K subscribers, 82 videos and 2,180,761 views; its recent 3D Shorts range from 263 to 7.9K views, so the channel needs a broader, more searchable promise than niche insect anatomy.
How a Hen Makes a Perfect Egg Every Day (SP CLASSES) reached 6,694,593 views at 149 s, a 2,138x multiple over its surrounding uploads; narration is Hindi, so the English 9:16 slot is open.
The competitor devotes its full 149 s to the five oviduct stages and closes on unfertilised eggs; its structure proves demand for the assembly-line framing but leaves a 30 s fast-cut version untaken.

The whole egg takes about 23 to 26 hours from ovulation to laying; the magnum adds roughly 40% of the albumen in about 3 hours, and the uterus or shell gland holds the egg for 18 to 20 hours while adding the shell and the rest of the albumen.
One egg needs about 2.5 g of calcium while a hen can absorb roughly 2.0 g per day from feed, so part of every shell is drawn from medullary bone.
Because calcification alone takes 18 to 20 hours, the cycle cannot run much under a day; one egg per day is close to a hard biological ceiling.
A hen lays without a rooster; unfertilised eggs are the normal supermarket case.

A 6 s kinesin Short reached 19,103,948 views and a 62 s atom-zoom Short reached 9,959,323 views, showing that unseen-microscale mechanics clear millions, but neither fits the Monarch Cam animal-ability spine as cleanly as the oviduct clock.
Competitor thumbnails could not be audited: i.ytimg.com returns SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL from this sandbox and image search returned unrelated stock art. No palette, contrast or caption claim is made.
All frames must be labelled as original illustrative 3D; no real dissection or lab footage is claimed.
